sentences.text: A cartesian point view uses point marks, with x-position encoding Income and defining Income Level bands. Y-position encodes Lifespan, point size encodes Population, color encodes Region, and text labels encode country.

The quantitative variables are Income (GDP per capita, $ per year, price adjusted), Lifespan (years), and Population (million); categorical variables are country, Region, and Income Level, with four displayed Income Level bands.

Across Africa, Americas, Asia and Oceania, and Europe, country marks form an elongated lower-left-to-upper-right band across Income and Lifespan. Regional extrema place Singapore highest for Income and Lifespan, while Central African Republic is lowest for Lifespan; its supporting mark, point 171, records 55.486939539350665 years.

The point encodings support a strong positive but curved Income–Lifespan association that flattens at higher Income. Singapore in Asia and Oceania is the visually supported global maximum for both Income (137896.54983446767 GDP per capita, $ per year, price adjusted) and Lifespan (85.7153242230327 years), while Central African Republic in Africa is the global Lifespan minimum at 55.486939539350665 years.
